(Torrance, California) | college = [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]] (2017–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–2022]] | team1 = [[Capital City Go-Go]] | years2 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2022|start}} | team2 = [[Washington Wizards]] | years3 = [[2022-23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team3 = Capital City Go-Go | years4 = [[2022-23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team4 = [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] | years5 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–2024]] | team5 = [[Maine Celtics]] | years6 = 2024 | team6 = [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] | years7 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team7 = Maine Celtics | years8 = 2025 | team8 = [[BC Oostende|Filou Oostende]] | years9 = 2025–present | team9 = [[Niners Chemnitz]] | highlights = * Second-team All-[[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]] (2021) }} '''Jordan Schakel''' (born June 13, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Niners Chemnitz]] of German [[Basketball Bundesliga]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State Aztecs]]. Throughout his college career, Schakel scored 225 field goals from behind the 3-point line, ranking third in SDSU's history, and ended his college career with a total 1,034 points. He averaged 42.7 percent from behind the three-point line and 46.11 percent during his final year, ranking third nationally in the 2020–21 season. Schakel graduated with a degree in marketing from the [[SDSU Fowler College of Business]] and was named a Scholar Athlete in each semester. Before joining the Aztecs, Schakel graduated from [[Bishop Montgomery High School]] in [[Torrance, California]]. In high school, he was part of the team that won the state's [[California high school basketball championship#Boys State Champions|Division IV Championship]] of [[California Interscholastic Federation]] in his freshman year and, as a senior, helped his team win the Open Division Championship, the top high school basketball title in California. Schakel was ranked by [[ESPN]] as a 4-star recruit of the class of 2017{{cite web|title=Basketball Recruiting - Jordan Schakel - Player Profiles - ESPN|url=https://insider.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/evaluation/_/id/189441/jordan-schakel|website=ESPN.com|access-date=May 26, 2021}} and was named to the first-team All-CIF, All-Del Rey League, and All-CIF Southern Section Open Division, and the ''[[Daily Breeze]]''{{'s}} All-Area First Team. ==Early life== Schakel was born on June 13, 1998, in [[Torrance, California]].{{Cite web|title=Jordan Schakel Player Profile, San Diego State, NCAA Stats, Game Logs, Bests, Awards|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Jordan-Schakel/Summary/88872|access-date=May 12, 2021|website=RealGM}} He began playing [[American football|football]]{{cite web|last1=Northcutt|first1=Sydney|date=November 10, 2017|title=Sharpshooting Schakel brings winning ways to San Diego|url=https://thedailyaztec.com/85813/sports/sharpshooting-schakel-brings-winning-ways-to-san-diego/|access-date=February 24, 2021|website=[[The Daily Aztec]]}} and basketball at an early age. In third grade, he played in a local [[3x3 (basketball)|3-on-3]] basketball tournament in [[Long Beach, California]].{{Cite web|last=Zeigler|first=Mark|date=February 25, 2017|title=Seiko, Schakel bring hate-to-lose attitude to Aztecs|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/sd-sp-azhoops-20170224-story.html|access-date=May 12, 2021|website=San Diego Union-Tribune|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|last=Zeigler|first=Mark|date=July 21, 2016|title=SDSU basketball gets commit from 4-star prospect|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/sdut-sdsu-basketball-jordan-schakel-commit-2016jul21-story.html|access-date=May 12, 2021|website=San Diego Union-Tribune|language=en-US}} ==High school career== As a freshman on the [[Bishop Montgomery High School]] basketball team, Schakel played in the [[California high school basketball championship|CIF State Division IV Championship]]. As a sophomore, his team instead took part in the top Open Division championships. The freshman scored 106 points, with 12 steals, 19 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]], 27 three-pointers, and only 9 [[Turnover (basketball)|turnovers]] in 455 minutes of playing time for the season.{{Cite web|title=Jordan Schakel: Summary|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaab/players/141235/|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=Yahoo! Sports|language=en-US}} After winning [[2018 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|the Mountain West Conference tournament]], his team qualified as 11 seed at the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA tournament]] but lost in the first round to 21-seed [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]] 67–65.{{Cite web|last=Zeigler|first=Mark|date=March 11, 2018|title=Aztecs get 11 seed, draw Houston in NCAA Tournament|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/sd-sp-sdsu-aztecs-basketball-ncaa-tournament-san-diego-20180311-story.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109020055/https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/sd-sp-sdsu-aztecs-basketball-ncaa-tournament-san-diego-20180311-story.html|archive-date=November 9, 2020|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=San Diego Union-Tribune|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|last=Boone|first=Kyle|date=March 15, 2018|title=Houston vs. San Diego State's insane final minute makes Rob Gray a March Madness hero|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/houston-vs-san-diego-states-insane-final-minute-makes-rob-gray-a-march-madness-hero/|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=CBSSports.com|language=en}} As a sophomore in the [[2018–19 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|2018–19 season]], Schakel started in 16 of the 28 games in which he participated, averaging 23.3 minutes per game. He scored 207 points, with 22 steals, 30 assists, 44 three-pointers, and only 15 turnovers in 651 minutes of playing time for the season. The team made it to the final game of the [[2019 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|2019 Mountain West Conference tournament]] but lost to Utah State and failed to qualify for the NCAA tournament.{{Cite web|last=Kragthorpe|first=Kurt|date=March 16, 2019|title=Utah State books trip to NCAA Tournament by beating San Diego State 64-57 in the MW title game|url=https://sltrib.com/sports/2019/03/17/utah-state-books-trip|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=The Salt Lake Tribune|language=en-US}} As a junior in the [[2019–20 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|2019–20 season]], Schakel became a regular starter, averaging 10 points and 3.4 rebounds per game. He started in 31 of the 32 games he participated in and recorded 27 steals, 18 assists, 2 blocks, and only 17 turnovers in 850 minutes of playing time.{{cite web |title=Jordan Schakel - Men's Basketball |url=https://goaztecs.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jordan-schakel/6602 |website=SDSU Athletics |access-date=February 24, 2021}} On February 12, 2020, SDSU clinched the Mountain West Conference regular-season title.{{Cite web|last=Zeigler|first=Mark|date=February 12, 2020|title=Aztecs lock down Lobos in second half, clinch Mountain West title|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2020-02-11/san-diego-state-basketball-new-mexico-mountain-west-undefeated-champions|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=San Diego Union-Tribune|language=en-US}} The Aztecs only lost a single game in the regular season.{{Cite web|last=Associated Press|date=February 23, 2020|title=UNLV hands No. 4 San Diego State its first loss, 66-63|url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/02/22/unlv-hands-no-4-san-diego-state-its-first-loss-66-63/|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=NBC Sports|language=en-US}} The team had its second loss in the finals of the [[2021 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|2020 Mountain West Conference tournament]] and were projected to be a top seed in the NCAA tournament before it was [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports#Basketball|cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic]].{{Cite web|date=February 10, 2020|title=Aztecs Improve to 24-0; Projected No. 1 Seed in NCAA Tournament|url=https://newscenter.sdsu.edu/sdsu_newscenter/news_story.aspx?sid=77887|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=SDSU NewsCenter|language=en|archive-date=May 26, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526161704/https://newscenter.sdsu.edu/sdsu_newscenter/news_story.aspx?sid=77887|url-status=dead}}{{Cite web|last=Associated Press|date=November 26, 2020|title=Mitchell, Schakel lead SDSU to 73-58 win over No. 22 UCLA|url=https://wtop.com/ncaa-basketball/2020/11/mitchell-schakel-lead-sdsu-to-73-58-win-over-no-22-ucla/|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=WTOP|language=en|archive-date=May 26, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526161703/https://wtop.com/ncaa-basketball/2020/11/mitchell-schakel-lead-sdsu-to-73-58-win-over-no-22-ucla/|url-status=dead}} In [[2017–18 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|2020–21 season]], Schakel scored on 46.11 percent of his 3-pointer attempts, ranking third in the nation.{{Cite web|date=May 8, 2020|title=NCAA College Men's Basketball DI current individual Stats - Three-point Field-goal Percentage|url=https://www.ncaa.com/stats/basketball-men/d1/current/individual/143|url-status=live|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=NCAA.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526160559/https://www.ncaa.com/stats/basketball-men/d1/current/individual/143|archive-date=May 26, 2021|language=en}} He was twice named Mountain West Conference's Player of the Week during the season.{{Cite web|last=Zeigler|first=Mark|date=February 15, 2021|title=Aztecs back in AP basketball Top 25; Jordan Schakel earns MW honor|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2021-02-15/san-diego-state-sdsu-aztecs-basketball-associated-press-top-25-polls-rankings|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210217234947/https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2021-02-15/san-diego-state-sdsu-aztecs-basketball-associated-press-top-25-polls-rankings|archive-date=February 17, 2021|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=San Diego Union-Tribune|language=en-US}} On January 4, 2021, Schakel recorded 28 points and nine rebounds in a 78–65 win over [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]]. He made eight three-pointers, the second-most in a game in program history.{{cite web |last1=Finley |first1=Andrew |title=Schakel has a career night as men's basketball rebounds versus Colorado State |url=https://thedailyaztec.com/103443/sports/schakel-has-a-career-night-as-mens-basketball-rebounds-versus-colorado-state/ |website=[[The Daily Aztec]] |access-date=February 24, 2021 |date=January 4, 2021}} On March 3, 2021, SDSU clinched the Mountain West Conference regular-season title for the second year in row.{{Cite web|last=Zeigler|first=Mark|date=March 4, 2021|title=Aztecs capture second straight Mountain West title with win at UNLV|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2021-03-03/san-diego-state-sdsu-aztecs-basketball-unlv-rebels-mountain-west-championship|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210310003743/https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2021-03-03/san-diego-state-sdsu-aztecs-basketball-unlv-rebels-mountain-west-championship|archive-date=March 10, 2021|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=San Diego Union-Tribune|language=en-US}} At the [[2021 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|2021 Mountain West Conference tournament]], the team beat Utah State 68–57 to win the conference tournament championship, with Schakel named to the All-Tournament Team.{{Cite web|date=March 14, 2021|title=San Diego State Set for NCAA Tournament After Winning Conference Crown Over Utah State, 68-57|url=https://timesofsandiego.com/sports/2021/03/13/san-diego-state-set-for-ncaa-tournament-after-winning-conference-crown-over-utah-state-68-57/|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=Times of San Diego|language=en-US}} The Aztecs were seeded 6th in the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2021 NCAA tournament]] but lost in the first round to 11-seed [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]].{{Cite web|last=Associated Press|title=Syracuse Orange vs. San Diego State Aztecs Live Score and Stats - March 19, 2021 Gametracker|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/gametracker/recap/NCAAB_20210319_CUSE@SDGST/|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=CBSSports.com|language=en}} Throughout his college career, Schakel scored 225 field goals from behind the 3-point line, ranking third in SDSU's history, and ended his college career with a total 1,034 points.{{Cite web|last=Zeigler|first=Mark|date=March 29, 2021|title=Aztecs' Jordan Schakel makes it official: He's turning pro|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2021-03-29/san-diego-state-sdsu-aztecs-basketball-jordan-schakel-pro-nba-recruiting-transfers-joel-mensah|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210329234918/https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2021-03-29/san-diego-state-sdsu-aztecs-basketball-jordan-schakel-pro-nba-recruiting-transfers-joel-mensah|archive-date=March 29, 2021|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=San Diego Union-Tribune|language=en-US}} He finished his career as SDSU's all-time leader in career [[Free throw|free-throw]] percentage at 87 percent.{{Cite web|last=Betz|first=Kyle|date=May 14, 2021|title=Column: Jordan Schakel and Matt Mitchell rank among best duos in program history|url=https://thedailyaztec.com/105861/sports/column-jordan-schakel-and-matt-mitchell-rank-among-best-duos-in-program-history/|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=The Daily Aztec}} San Diego State announced that Schakel will participate in the State Farm College 3-point Championships. A few hours later, Schakel announced he would pursue a professional career by entering the [[2021 NBA draft]]. He graduated with a degree in marketing from the [[SDSU Fowler College of Business]] and was named a Scholar Athlete in each semester of college. ==Professional career== ===Washington Wizards / Capital City Go-Go (2021–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Schakel joined the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|title=Warriors Announce 2021 Summer League Roster, Presented by Oracle|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/summer-league-roster-20210802|work=NBA.com|date=August 2, 2021|access-date=September 24, 2021}} and later joined the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the Las Vegas Summer League. The Kings, including Schakel, won the Summer League Championship in 2021.{{cite news|first=Mark|last=Zeigler|title=SDSU's Schakel, Mitchell go undrafted but not unsigned|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2021-07-30/san-diego-state-sdsu-aztecs-basketball-jordan-schakel-golden-state-warriors-matt-mitchell-san-antonio-spurs|work=[[The San Diego Union-Tribune]]|date=July 30, 2021|access-date=August 3, 2021}} On September 21, 2021, he signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite tweet|author=Washington Wizards|number=1440478129382846464|title=OFFICIAL: We've signed the following players to Exhibit 10 contracts: □ Jaime Echenique □ Jordan Goodwin □ Jay Huff □ Jordan Schakel|user=WashWizards|date=September 21, 2021|access-date=September 24, 2021}} However, he was waived by the Wizards on October 13.{{cite web|title=Jordan Schakel: Parts ways with Wizards|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jordan-schakel-parts-ways-with-wizards/|website=CBS Sports|date=October 13, 2021|access-date=October 15, 2021}} Thirteen days later, Schakel joined the [[Capital City Go-Go]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web|title=Go-Go Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/go-go-announce-training-camp-roster/n-5758523|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 26, 2021|access-date=October 26, 2021}} In 14 games, he averaged 13.8 points and 3.2 rebounds per game while shooting .396 from three-point range. He led the NBA G League in made threes during that stretch with 44.{{cite web|title=Wizards sign Jordan Schakel to 10-Day contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-jordan-schakel-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 22, 2021|access-date=December 22, 2021}} On December 22, 2021, Schakel signed a 10-day contract with the [[Washington Wizards]]. On January 1, 2022, Schakel was reacquired and activated by the [[Capital City Go-Go]] after his 10-day contract expired.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 1, 2022|access-date=January 1, 2022}} On March 9, 2022, Schakel signed a
